verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev's own docs claim elastic, managed auto-scaling 'with nothing to provision' and processing millions of tasks. Durable tasks are said to survive crashes, and retries with exponential backoff are documented. That covers the scaling core only at a marketing-claim level. Missing for 10: documentation of adding workers to raise throughput (including on self-hosted fleets), explicit load-balancing of tasks across workers, explicit recovery semantics when a worker is lost, and independent or hands-on corroboration of scaling behavior.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, throughput scales by adding workers — the platform load-balances tasks across the fleet and tolerates worker loss

citations.quote: Trigger.dev is a managed compute platform where those same jobs get durability, observability, and auto-scaling with nothing to provision.
